ops.oldText: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party.
ops.newText: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.

ops.text: IBM may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and MSL may not assign this Agreement to any IBM competitor.

ops.oldText: v) substantially all of the shares or assets of one Party are acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other Party.
ops.newText: v) substantially all of the shares or assets of MSL are acquired by an entity that competes directly with IBM.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We made consent to assignment subject to a reasonableness standard, added our customary carve-out permitting IBM to assign to an affiliate or successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, barred MSL from assigning to an IBM competitor, and narrowed the competitor-acquisition termination trigger so MSL cannot exit on an IBM change of control.
proposal.summary: Add a reasonableness standard to consent in 16.2, insert an IBM affiliate/successor assignment carve-out and a bar on MSL assigning to an IBM competitor, and narrow the 5.1(b)(v) competitor-acquisition trigger to MSL.

mappings.quote: MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM.

input.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party.
input.rationale:
Section 16.2 bars either Party from assigning without the other's prior written approval, with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out for IBM and no reasonableness standard except for MSL Related Company assignments, which is walk-away territory; Section 5.1(b)(v) also lets MSL terminate on an IBM change of control. The redline adds a reasonableness standard, IBM's affiliate/successor carve-out and a bar on MSL assigning to an IBM competitor, and narrows the competitor-acquisition trigger to MSL, preserving IBM's own termination right and the favourable Section 16.5 mechanic.</rationale>
